clauses.text: Every creature, including every player character, has a tag in the rules that identifies the type of creature it is.
Most player characters are of the Humanoid type.
These are the game’s creature types:
The types don’t have rules themselves, but some rules in the game affect creatures of certain types in different ways.

ambiguities.quote: has a tag in the rules that identifies the type of creature it is
ambiguities.reading_a: Each creature has exactly one creature type from the list, and any parenthetical stat-block descriptor (such as a subgroup) isn't a type.
ambiguities.reading_b: A creature may carry more than one type tag, so a rule that names any of its types affects it.
ambiguities.proposed_ruling: Reading A: each creature has exactly one creature type from the 14 listed. A stat-block descriptor in parentheses is not a creature type for rules that name types.

ambiguities.quote: These are the game’s creature types:
ambiguities.reading_a: The list is closed: the engine rejects any creature type not among the 14.
ambiguities.reading_b: The list is only illustrative, so content may add other types.
ambiguities.proposed_ruling: Reading A: the 14 listed types are the only valid values. Content that uses any other type is refused as a data error.

gaps.quote: Every creature, including every player character, has a tag in the rules that identifies the type of creature it is.
gaps.explanation: This unit doesn't say whether a creature's type can change, or which type applies while an effect replaces or alters its form (for example, taking on a Beast's stat block). Only the rules that change a form can answer that.

traps.quote: Most player characters are of the Humanoid type.
traps.note: In 2014, a player character's type came from its race, with Humanoid subtype tags in parentheses such as '(elf)' or '(goblinoid)'. In 2024 the term is 'species', and a parenthetical tag on a stat block isn't a separate type. Don't model a Humanoid subtype as a creature type.

output.summary: Glossary definition. Every creature, player characters included, has a creature-type tag. The 14 types are listed, most player characters are Humanoid, and the types carry no rules themselves: only other rules that name a type make it matter. There are no thresholds, relations or conflicts. The two ambiguities are minor: whether a creature has exactly one type, and whether the list is closed.
